item.title: [ 58] House advances bill barring sitting Congress members from buying stocks
item.description:
https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/22/house-congressional-stock-trading.html?msockid=196670d327c565552f78675826d66426

The U.S. House advanced legislation on Wednesday that would stop members of Congress from buying individual stocks while in office, taking the first meaningful action on an issue that has dogged lawmakers for years.

The bill passed on a vote of 232-198, with more than a dozen Democrats joining Republicans in support.

There is broad public support for a ban on members of Congress trading while in office, as lawmakers’ well-timed trades and booming portfolios have raised insider trading concerns among ethics watchdogs and drawn intense public scrutiny going back decades.

But the GOP-led legislation advanced by the House, dubbed the Stop Insider Trading Act, falls well short of what the most vocal advocates of a congressional trading ban have called for. And many Democrats had lined up against the proposal.

“I’m very disappointed in it. It’s a stock trading ban that still allows stock trading. It’s a weak bill,” Rep. Seth Magaziner, D-R.I., part of a bipartisan coalition that has advocated for a more thorough ban, told CNBC.

item.title: [ 70] Suspect in attack on federal building was targeting ICE
item.description:
https://www.fox5ny.com/news/army-vet-was-targeting-ice-fiery-attack-outside-nyc-federal-building-fbi
NEW YORK CITY - A morning commute in Lower Manhattan erupted into chaos after a suspect ignited a fire, set off commercial fireworks and brandished a pellet gun directly outside 26 Federal Plaza, a high-security complex that houses offices for the FBI, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and federal immigration courts.

The suspect, who was quickly taken into custody by federal security officers, has been identified by authorities as 43-year-old Andrew Arrabaca

Officials say Arrabaca, a former U.S. Army Patriot missile systems mechanic with ties to both Poughkeepsie and Harlem, arrived at the federal building with a variety of weapons and incendiary materials.

He was armed with six incendiary devices, commercial-grade fireworks, a bucket of suspected gasoline, two axes, a hammer, a machete, three knives and airsoft pellet guns/rifles.
Law enforcement officials characterized the suspect as an anti-government extremist driven by opposition to federal immigration enforcement.

"He came armed with bad intentions, looking to injure people and harm people," said James Barnacle, Assistant Director in Charge of the FBI’s New York Field Office. "He is an anti-American, anti-government extremist. We know that from what he said post-arrest, and we know that from the actions he tried to take."

item.title: [ 38] AIPAC Is Losing Its Sway Over Democrats
item.description:
The pro-Israel group’s absolutist stance has alienated even moderate Democrats who support the Jewish state.

https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/aipac-losing-sway-over-democrats-111559774.html

WASHINGTON — In 2024, a super PAC allied with the American Israel Public Affairs Committee spent $4 million to boost then-state Sen. Sarah Elfreth in a contested Democratic primary in Maryland. It’s not an exaggeration to say the money was decisive: It was more than twice as much as Elfreth’s campaign raised and spent.

It was one of a string of wins for AIPAC in Democratic primaries, starting in 2022, when it backed candidates who would keep military aid flowing to Israel. The group has long been clear about what it expects from candidates it backs: There should be no conditions on aid to Israel under any circumstances.

But last week, Elfreth was one of the 10 Democrats who voted “present” on a symbolic amendment to cut off aid to Israel, signaling an unwillingness to shoot down the effort completely. Another 21 Democrats who had received financial backing from AIPAC voted for the amendment. Altogether, 103 Democrats voted for the amendment in a rebuke of Israel and its prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, who has overseen a war in Gaza that has led to more than 70,000 deaths.

In a lengthy statement, Elfreth called the vote a ploy by House Republican leaders to divide Democrats. She said the amendment was poorly written, but also, regarding Israel, that “the current dynamics of our allyship are not sustainable for the region and our nation.”

AIPAC appeared to cut off fundraising support to the Democrats who voted yes. One of them, Rep. Pat Ryan (D-N.Y.), said he welcomed the consequences.

item.title: [113] New York sculptor spent $100,000 to make a Charlie Kirk statue no one wants to buy
item.description:
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jul/20/sculptor-charlie-kirk-statue-new-york

A New York sculptor has been left furious after spending $100,000 of his own money to build a lifesize statue of Charlie Kirk, only to find that no one wants to buy it.

Sergio Furnari, originally from Italy, had hoped the statue of the deceased far-right activist, which he intends to display in Times Square, would raise “millions” of dollars. Instead, he said he has been inundated by messages from people saying they intend to urinate on the sculpture.

To add injury to insult, Furnari recently broke his foot working on the statue, after tripping over a roll of tape in his studio.

“Is it cursed? Maybe. I don’t know,” he told the Guardian.

Kirk, a far-right political figure who served as a sort of Pied Piper for young Republicans through his Turning Point USA foundation, was shot dead in September last year. He was known for his racist and bigoted views, using his podcast to claim that “prowling Blacks go around for fun to go target white people” and speculating: “If I see a Black pilot, I’m going to be like: ‘Boy, I hope he’s qualified.’”

Despite, or perhaps because of, such beliefs, Kirk became a hugely celebrated and influential figure in Maga circles. In New York City, one of the most diverse, and Democratic, cities in the US, Kirk is far less popular.

Furnari said he did not agree with Kirk on “certain issues”.

item.title: [ 38] DOJ’s Reflecting Pool “Vandalism” Case Falls Apart With Pool Draining
item.description:
https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2026/07/20/reflecting-pool-repairs-could-undermine-case-against-former-olympian-judge-says/

Repair work at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool done after a former Olympic canoeist was accused of damaging it could jeopardize the government’s case against him, a D.C. Superior Court judge warned Monday.

The government is “operating at its own peril,” said Judge Todd E. Edelman, if the Reflecting Pool is altered or not preserved before the defense’s expert has a chance to sample it.

Earlier this month, a grand jury indicted David Hearn, 67, for allegedly vandalizing the Reflecting Pool. Hearn pleaded not guilty.

On Thursday, defense attorneys for Hearn filed a motion to dismiss the indictment against him, alleging the government failed to preserve the section of Reflecting Pool liner that Hearn is charged with damaging, according to court documents.

“Despite the importance of the pool liner to the case, in the brief period since June 19, 2026, the same government that presented and returned the indictment against Mr. Hearn has fenced off the scene, begun draining the pool yet again, and publicly announced its intention to repair the very liner whose condition is at issue,” attorneys said in the court document.

They sent an attorney to the Reflecting Pool for an inspection and “confirmed that spoliation of evidence has taken place,” according to the motion.

Hearn’s defense attorneys said that Hearn is entitled to use his own experts to test the Reflecting Pool but that “he cannot do so once the government has resurfaced the Reflecting Pool,” according to the motion.

During a status hearing Monday, Edelman denied the defense’s motion but questioned the government as to whether the status quo of the Reflecting Pool has been maintained.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Kevin Reddington and Kadian Carter said at the hearing that they were not sure whether the affected area had been touched.

Sorry if I've just insulted your favorite /out/ location but a few months ago I made a thread with mountains captioned as Appalachian locations and nobody could tell something is wrong, even though one of the pics was from Czechia, others were from Poland and none was actually from Appalachia. To make things even worse, I had to stop myself from using the highest parts of Carpathians cause they just look too stunning to be Appalachia. Basically Appalachia looks like one of these mountain locations I visit because they're cheaper than ones with more dramatic landscape and if I wanted to go on holyday by plane, I certainly wouldn't choose Georgia (Appalachia) over Yosemite or Georgia (Caucasus).

But maybe I'm wrong and someone who actually visited Appalachia can tell me why are they truly special?

item.title: [ 97] Tent General
item.description:
Post your tents, your tentfu, which will be your next acquisition, etc

I currently have my first tent (a typical cheap igloo camping tent, Hummer Igloo 3+) and 2 ultra light 3 season tents (forclaz mt900 tarp tent for 1 and 2 persons). I have used the latter in high mountain before, during summer (which is still cold), but usually in this part of Los Andes the wind is too strong for my tent. So I'm planning to buy a 4 season tent more appropriate for high-altitude and strong winds.
Around here most people use the mountaineering line of Doite, pic related would be the one appropriate for my needs. The thing is that here tents are particularly expensive (that one costs +400usd), and I think I might be able to buy something half that price in the US, but I'm not familiar with US brands. Which one would you recommend?
